draft.body:
# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. draft.body:
# My shuttle memo notes

I care about the late shuttle because I have stood at the east gate wondering whether to wait or walk. I want the memo to admit that this is my starting point. It is not a campus-wide survey. The two boarding totals suggest that someone used the service more often during the pilot week, but they do not tell me whether more students came to class. I should not make a number answer a question it was never asked.

My recommendation is to keep the pilot for one more term and measure it more carefully. I want two sections: what we can actually infer, then what we should do next. Please keep the uncertainty visible. Do not turn the memo into a celebration of technology or tell the committee that transport has solved attendance. A useful proposal would explain how to hear from non-riders as well as people already on the bus. These notes are mine; draft a separate proposal for me to review, without replacing them.

No attendance data were collected during either week [@lyra:1]. The academic schedules also differed between weeks, and the pilot was not randomized. Consequently, the observed shift in ridership raises the question of who is using the service, but it cannot establish a causal link between shuttle availability and class attendance. I want this paragraph to keep my uncertainty visible rather than sound more certain than the evidence allows.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: I recommend we keep the shuttle running for one more term, not to prove success, but to gather better data. Since the current survey only includes riders [@lyra:2], any conclusion about overall demand would be premature. I do not yet know how much unused demand exists or whether the late departure actually changed attendance patterns. The pilot should continue under the condition that we fix this measurement gap. My goal is to determine if more students can access the service, not to celebrate the existing program. I can accept a conditional extension only if we agree to treat the next term as a test of access, not a confirmation of the status quo.

live_draft_blocks.heading: Recommendation
live_draft_blocks.content: That extension gives us a concrete task: survey the students who did not ride. The existing sample of 18 voluntary responses excludes everyone who stayed home [@lyra:2], so we currently cannot say whether those students lack access, lack need, or simply prefer walking. I propose adding a short, optional survey distributed to non-riders at the end of the extended term. I am not claiming this will solve the problem, only that it will tell us whether the barrier is time, route, or indifference. If the responses show widespread interest we can justify expansion; if they do not, we can end the pilot with a clearer rationale than we have now. I want that answer before we decide anything else.
